headline: Learned models stratify disease risk from blood, imaging, and omics data
label: Ml For Biomedical Data Stratification
summary: Deep and foundation models are being benchmarked against clinical baselines and tested for replicability across cohorts.
synthesis: The dominant thread is machine learning applied to routine or high-dimensional biomedical measurements, with evaluation increasingly framed as explicit comparison against established baselines and as replicability across cohorts. NORMA, a conditional transformer, generates personalized blood biomarker reference intervals from patient history and population priors. A MASLD study compares FIB-4 with a shallow-deep neural network, TabPFN, and fine-tuned GPT-4o on biopsy-confirmed external cohorts. MetAgeFormer pretrains a transformer by self-supervised learning on UK Biobank NMR metabolomics to derive aging clocks and metabolic subtypes. A replicability study assesses unsupervised deep-learning brain MRI phenotypes across seeds, splits, and cohorts using CKA, KCCA, and loci overlap. Other items address Parkinson's MRI subtyping, retinal imaging for systemic risk, tabular-to-image layout for multiclass classification, and single-patch prediction of spatial gene expression from H&E images.
